report.body:
Police in Água Clara, Mato Grosso do Sul, detained five men in a joint operation
against drug trafficking that began on the night of 4 November 2026. Four
were arrested in flagrante on suspicion of drug trafficking and association for
trafficking, while the fifth was captured on an outstanding arrest warrant.
The first suspect, a 30-year-old man, was taken to the Água Clara police
station. Officers said he had already been under investigation by the Civil
Police's General Investigations Section (SIG).

The operation started after military police received a tip that a man was
selling drugs from a white VW Gol in the Jardim das Palmeiras neighbourhood. The driver tried to flee when he saw the patrol car and was caught after a
chase lasting a few blocks. In the car officers found a portion of a
cocaine-like substance, and at the man's home they seized portions of marijuana,
a precision scale, packaging materials and money. A Civil Police
investigation identified a second address used to store a larger quantity of
drugs. There teams found 59 tablets of a marijuana-like substance weighing
about 54 kilograms. Two men aged 18 and 20 were arrested at that address. A third suspect, 22, was later stopped with about 500 grams of marijuana
and another precision scale. Police also seized 120 grams of cocaine in 19
portions. The final balance was about 54.64 kilograms of drugs including
marijuana and cocaine, along with a car, a motorcycle, three precision scales,
three mobile phones, packaging and about R$250 in cash.

Police said the main stash was hidden in a wooded area near the MS-324 highway. All those involved were taken to the Água Clara Civil Police station for
legal proceedings. The operation involved both the Military Police and the
Civil Police.

Military police in Mojuí dos Campos, Pará, arrested João Victor Castro on the
afternoon of 12 November 2026 after finding him with substances resembling
marijuana and cocaine. The stop was made around 17:45 at the junction of
Travessa São Sebastião and Rua Joana D'Arc in Mojuí dos Campos. Officers of
the 35º BPM said he was accompanied by his wife, who told them more illicit
material was at the couple's home on Rua Almirante Barroso in the Cidade Alta 2
neighbourhood. G1 reports that the man became nervous at the approach of a
patrol car and was found with the first portions of drug. His companion
told police he worked in drug trafficking in the area, and he confessed and said
he kept more cocaine and marijuana at home.

At the house officers found R$301 in cash, 31 wrappers of a substance analogous
to cocaine and 12 wrappers of a substance analogous to marijuana. The
material list also records one portion of greenish substance similar to
marijuana. Officers also found a portion of drug outside the packaging,
various drug-packaging materials and a black Samsung A14 mobile phone. G1
gives the same counts as 31 packets of cocaine, 12 portions of marijuana and
R$300 in cash, describing the drugs as ready for commercialisation.

The man was given a voice of arrest and taken with the seized material to the
police station in Santarém, where legal procedures were carried out. The
suspect and the seized material were forwarded for the proper procedures at the
16ª Seccional de Polícia Civil de Santarém, and he was placed at the disposal of
the judiciary.

tool without lawful justification. Ahl Masr said anti-narcotics officers in

report.body:
Mossos d'Esquadra detectives arrested seven men aged 29 to 55 on 1 October 2026
in an industrial warehouse in Cabanes, Girona, over suspected links to a
drug-trafficking organisation. Officers found the seven men unloading
pallets from a trailer with the intention of loading the hashish into vans for
distribution, with support from the ARRO unit in Girona, the Catalan government
said. The seven were placed at the disposal of the investigating court in
Figueres, and the investigation remains open with further arrests not ruled out.

Officers seized 8,025 kg of hashish at the warehouse, according to the Catalan
government. The drug was hidden in large raffia sacks filled with rubber
crumb among the trailer's cargo, a method used to evade police and customs
checks. The authorities valued the seized hashish at more than 16.2 million
euros on the illicit market.

The investigation began in June 2026 after Mossos officers stopped a van
carrying nearly 2,400 kg of hashish in Viladecans, Barcelona, which was linked
to the Cabanes warehouse. In early October surveillance recorded repeated
movements of people and vans, the arrival of an articulated truck and the
swapping of licence plates before the trailer was driven inside. The Mossos
said the haul was a significant share of the nearly 14,900 kg of hashish they
had seized during 2026 by 1 October. During the search officers also found
a firearm in one of the detainees' vans.

report.body:
Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta carrying a
stash of hashish hidden in a sophisticated false bottom. Officers
intercepted the truck on the port road at the Muelle de Poniente and searched it
with support from the UPR prevention unit and the canine group. They found
the hashish and detained the driver, showing him the drugs found in the vehicle
he was driving.

The truck appeared empty and was heading toward boarding for Spain when a
specialist drugs dog alerted, prompting an exhaustive hours-long search inside
and outside the vehicle. After the hours-long detailed inspection, officers
found a large number of bags full of hashish inside the truck's structure.
Officers recovered numerous bags of hashish from the trailer's false bottom,
with first estimates putting the haul above 300 kilograms although police gave
no official weight. The submitted account describes the seizure as about
300 kilograms of hashish arriving from Morocco.

The handcuffed driver was taken to police headquarters and placed under
investigation for an offence against public health. On Sunday 15 November the driver was brought before a judicial authority, which issued an order for his preventive detention for an offence against public health. Police link the
operation to open UDYCO investigations into groups moving hashish from Ceuta to
mainland Spain in heavy vehicles with hidden compartments.

report.title: Five arrested in Mallorca courier-hashish case; 60 kilos seized
report.summary: National Police concluded a months-long investigation into a Mallorca drug network with five arrests and 60 kilos of hashish seized, including a 24-kilo courier parcel. Searches of two homes found a compressed-air rifle, about 10,000 euros in cash, two kilos of cocaine and a hydraulic press; the case remains open.
report.body:
Officers of the National Police's Drugs and Organised Crime Unit (Udyco)
arrested at least three people on Mallorca who were storing almost 50 kilos of
hashish for sale. Those held were four men and one woman. Police said the months-long investigation ended with five arrests. The suspects received the hashish from the Spanish
mainland in courier parcels, according to the newspaper's case sources. The intercepted parcel contained 24 kilos of hashish and its recipient was arrested on suspicion of drug trafficking. The
arrests took place on Wednesday 4 November. Officers searched a home in
Marratxí, a municipality east of Palma, and another in a town in es Raiguer, the
district around the town of Inca. An investigating court in Palma declared
the case secret. Investigators had followed the suspects for some time;
over the previous months they had collected parcels of the drug from courier
companies and kept them at home for sale through others in the network.

In the Marratxí search, police found a large quantity of hashish in a chest
freezer and an air rifle. At the main suspect's home officers found 36 kilos of hashish, a compressed-air rifle with a silencer and about 10,000 euros in cash. Police put the total hashish seizure at 60 kilos. A woman was arrested there over her alleged link
to the criminal organisation and was released at the police station hours later. A man and a woman were arrested there on suspicion of drug trafficking and belonging to a criminal organisation. Two more people were arrested the same day, and all the suspects are
Spanish nationals. A fifth person was arrested for links to the case. A hydraulic press was found that police say was for compressing the cocaine. There they found two kilos of cocaine, prepared doses, cutting material, a 9mm pistol and a bow and arrows. At the second home, officers arrested another suspect they say guarded and transported the drugs.

The investigation is still open, further arrests are not ruled out, and the
suspects were due to appear before a Palma court in the coming hours. Officers from the Prevention and Reaction Unit, Grupo II de Estupefacientes and dog handlers also took part. Police say the group distributed the drugs to third parties for smaller-scale sale.

farms covering about eight acres at Yaruni Bend, Linden, in the Upper Demerara

Police in Pudukkottai, Tamil Nadu, arrested two women at the scene, Vasanthi and
Shanmugapriya — the niece of Vasanthi — both from the Thiruvappur Kovilpatti
area. Officers had stopped a suspicious luxury car travelling from Andhra
Pradesh towards Pudukkottai on Friday, 6 November 2026, and searched it.
Inside, they found ganja packets stacked in bundles in a hidden part of the car.

Police seized 26 kg of ganja that had been brought by car from Andhra Pradesh to
Pudukkottai. The car used in the smuggling was also seized, with the ganja
valued at about 13 lakh rupees (1.3 million rupees). A preliminary
investigation found that the two planned to supply local agents in Pudukkottai
and its surrounding areas.

circulation in the state. Police registered a case and are investigating
who was behind the interstate ganja network and who drove the car.

the Negombo Magistrate's Court on 15 October. The Police Narcotics Bureau

flat in Ajdabiya, detained two suspects and referred them to the Public
Prosecution. The suspects admitted what they were accused of during the
preliminary procedures before being sent to prosecutors. A security force
searched the flat only after verifying the information, the directorate said.

tablets at 250 milligrams each, and 16,500 Libyan dinars. The items had
been hidden inside a bag designed for carrying children.

kept in a flat on the third floor of a residential building and were about to be
moved to an unknown place to conceal a distribution operation. Officers
opened an inquiry, notified the heads of the criminal investigation department
and the investigation unit, and obtained legal authorisation before searching
the flat. The operation was described as part of security efforts against
drugs and psychotropic substances and against those possessing and distributing
them.
